list.title: Interest Rate:

list.title: Repayment Term:

list.title: Example:

related_questions.question: How much would a $5000 loan cost per month?

text_blocks.snippet: A $5,000 personal loan could cost anywhere from $112 to $359 per month, depending on the interest rate and loan term. For example, a two-year loan at a 7.80% interest rate could be around $226 per month, while a three-year loan at a 15% interest rate could be around $173 per month.
Here's a breakdown of factors influencing the monthly payment:

list.snippet: Interest Rate: Higher interest rates result in higher monthly payments.
Loan Term: Longer loan terms (more months) mean lower monthly payments, but you'll pay more interest overall.
APR: The Annual Percentage Rate (APR) includes fees and charges, potentially making it slightly higher than the interest rate.
A $5,000 loan with a 25% APR and a 60-month term would be approximately $147 per month, according to OneMain Financial.
A $5,000 loan with a 12.32% APR and a 48-month term would be around $132.46 per month, according to AOL.com.

text_blocks.snippet: To get a more precise estimate, you can use a personal loan calculator from online lenders like SoFi or OneMain Financial.
